subject: Re: Competitive match + packaging question for pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jsmith@acme-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Competitive match + packaging question for pilot

Connor —

Quick one: our procurement team pulled together a short cost comparison between Redwood and our incumbent (SprintScale). They can match the headline per-token rate if we sign a 12-month committed capacity bundle, but they won’t include the runtime and SLA credits Redwood is proposing.

Two asks from our side before we bring legal in:
- Can Redwood mirror the headline economics for the pilot (3mo pilot that could convert to 12mo) if we accept a packaging constraint (no more than 3 model variants in pilot)?
- If not, what mix of credits/one-time concessions can get us within 5% TCO for the first 12 months?

I attached the procurement worksheet (summary tab). Would appreciate a short note on what’s flexible and what isn’t — want to keep this tight.

Thanks,
Jordan
Procurement Lead
Acme Analytics

Attachments: procurement_workbook_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jsmith@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Competitive match + packaging question for pilot

Jordan —

Thanks for the worksheet and the clear asks. Short answers up front: we can get within the 5% TCO window using a blended approach (limited headline match + operational credits + onboarding support). Details below.

What we can do for the pilot (3 months, 3 model variants):
- Headline match: we can reduce the per-token rate to match SprintScale for the pilot workload up to an agreed token cap.
- Onboarding credit: one-time migration/onboarding credit to offset integration and egress (~$25k).
- SLA/latency credit: we can't fully eliminate SLAs from our premium package, but we can attach a temporary performance credit pool that kicks in for missed latency SLOs during the pilot.

Trade-offs / constraints:
- The headline match requires the 3-variant limit you mentioned — if you add unlocked variants mid-pilot we reserve the right to revisit pricing.
- Blended match assumes typical token profile (50% short-form, 50% long-form). If your usage skews heavy to long-form we’ll need to adjust.

I’ve attached a quick pricing_comparison_v3.xlsx with the blended math and a conservative TCO estimate stretched to 12 months (pilot + expected ramp).

Next step: if this is directionally okay, can we loop in Jonas (cc’d on the next mail) to approve the concession bucket? I’ll put legal on a tight timeline once we lock the commercials.

—Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: pricing_comparison_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Competitive match + packaging question for pilot

Connor / Hannah —

Saw Connor’s plan. Approve supporting a limited headline match for a 3-month pilot under these guardrails:
- Maximum concession bucket: $40k (includes onboarding credit + performance credit pool).
- Pilot commitment must include a clear conversion trigger (either usage threshold or signed 12-mo PO).
- No extensions of the 3-variant constraint without renewed approval.

Hannah — please prep a short SOW template with the conversion trigger language and a clause covering rollback to standard runtime rates if conversion does not happen within 30 days of pilot end.

Connor — you can offer the match within the concession bucket but don’t commit to anything that exceeds $40k total or extends SLAs beyond 90 days. If legal needs a pricing exhibit, Hannah should route it through me.

Jonas
Head of Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference

(No attachments)

From: Jordan Smith <jsmith@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Competitive match + packaging question for pilot

Connor —

Appreciate the quick turn. That concession bucket sounds workable to procurement. Two clarifications before I confirm to stakeholders: 
1) Can you confirm the token cap you used for the headline match math in your spreadsheet? We want to ensure it's enforceable (either by route-level caps or a usage appendix).
2) For the SLA credit pool: is that cash-back or service credit? Procurement prefers credits against invoices rather than one-off cash settlements.

If you can confirm those two items and send the draft SOW, I’ll pull legal in and aim to get a PO if the conversion trigger is acceptable.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks — answers inline below and attached a draft SOW + pricing exhibit for review.

1) Token cap enforcement: the pricing exhibit uses a route-level cap on the pilot deployment (configured in the contract as an appendix and programmatically enforced by our routing layer). We used a conservative 125M token cap per month for the blended model in the spreadsheet; the exhibit includes a monitoring hook and monthly reconciliation process.

2) SLA credit pool: we can make the pool invoice-creditable (applied against future invoices) rather than a cash settlement. The SOW language reflects that and specifies how credits are calculated and applied.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached proposed_sow_acme_draft.pdf and the pricing exhibit in pricing_comparison_v3.xlsx.
- If acceptable, confirm a target PO date and I’ll hold legal on a 5-business-day turnaround for first review.

If procurement wants, we can also schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the exhibit and the enforcement mechanics.

—Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
